Source of sample.evidence_source: The present investigation sought to further contribute to this flourishing line of research by attempting to both expand and deepen the scope of modern conceptualizations of positive body image to include more emergent, experientially-based constructs such as body image flexibility (Sandoz,Wilson,Merwin, & Kellum, 2013). We chose to evaluate the tenability of these models using a culturally-sensitive figure rating scale instrument (Kelly, Bulik, & Mazzeo, 2011; Pulvers et al., 2004) in a pre-college sample of Black older adolescent females. The extracted value is for Study X.

section_summary.extract_value: This introduction section discusses the growing scholarship on body appreciation and body image flexibility, emphasizing the distinction between negative and positive body image. It reviews existing literature on factors influencing the relationship between body dissatisfaction and positive body image, such as age and physical activity. The section then introduces the present investigation (Study X), which aims to explore whether BMI moderates the inverse associations between body dissatisfaction and both body appreciation and body image flexibility in a pre-college sample of Black older adolescent females.
